summary: Submitting a decisive positive control for the primary finding's necessary premise, attached to a child investigation of the explained parent. The parent account rests on the removal guard firing because the local progress entry disappears, and its remaining source-derived boundary was that a member kept in a configuration half should keep its gate armed; this experiment settles that boundary by construction. It runs the same three-node Node-API cluster, elects leader 1, proposes a joint-explicit removal of node 3 that is never left, waits until node 3's own configuration lists it in the outgoing half while still counting it as a voter, and then invokes Propose on node 3 with two comparisons: the invocation returned, and its payload was committed. The cited anchor is the LeaveJoint deletion of outgoing voters that are in neither the incoming half nor the learner set, which is exactly the transition the guard reacts to. Local verification of the new test shows the predicted difference: node 3 is an outgoing voter per its own status, its invocation returned in 0 ms with no error, and the payload was committed on all three nodes, while the witness scenario with the member dropped from both halves left the same invocation pending for its whole window. Both comparisons were dry-run through the framework's own comparator against the local event stream and evaluate as complete holds, so the successor receipt should be cleanly interpretable and will let the parent interpretation state the premise as witnessed rather than source-derived.
